evidence.methodology_note: Predeclared sampling rule (frozen before evidence collection): for metric.third_party_tool_availability, sample the externally-observable tool categories that the ecosystem.md rubric treats as standard third-party coverage classes for a mainstream language -- (1) IDE/editor support, (2) linter, (3) formatter, (4) static analysis / code-quality platform integration, (5) build-system support, (6) CI/CD platform support, (7) dominant web/server framework(s), (8) package repository / dependency management, (9) test framework ecosystem. Selection rule for which named tool represents each category: the tool with the highest GitHub-stars-based popularity among tools explicitly documented as Kotlin-compatible in official Kotlin/JetBrains documentation or the Awesome-Kotlin curated list, checked via a single web-search retrieval route per category, snapshot 2026-09-22. For metric.production_adoption_deployment_evidence, the predeclared rule is: search for (a) JetBrains' own official adoption statistics/surveys (highest-authority, language-vendor-independent measurement channel) and (b) named production deployments at large, independently verifiable companies cited by multiple independent secondary sources, retrieved via the same two-route search protocol (official survey + independent industry coverage) applied uniformly across languages in this evaluation. Same retrieval depth (up to 4 searches) and snapshot time applied for Kotlin as for other languages in this shard.

findings.citation: <cite index=7-2>On 7 May 2019, Google announced that Kotlin is now its preferred language for Android app developers.</cite> <cite index=24-2>As of 2024, over 95% of the top 1,000 Android apps on Google Play contain Kotlin code.</cite>

<cite index=19-1,19-5>In a recent study, the JetBrains Research team analyzed telemetry from IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate over a 20-month window, from November 2023 to June 2025, covering roughly 320,000 developers and 28 million development cycles.</cite>
findings.point: Independent large-scale telemetry evidence of real production usage (not self-report)

findings.citation: <cite index=21-1>JetBrains' 2025 developer ecosystem survey (24,534 developers across 194 countries) lists Kotlin as 6th in 'want to adopt next' and 8% of backend developers' primary language.</cite> <cite index=21-9>Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 results: Kotlin at 15th place (10.8% of respondents), 51% wanting to continue using it, among the most 'loved' languages.</cite>

metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Some cited company-adoption lists come from KMP-focused marketing/consultancy blogs (2026 SEO content) rather than primary company engineering blogs; these were corroborated across multiple independent sources but not verified against original company sources directly. JetBrains-sourced statistics (survey and telemetry) are vendor-provided, though the IntelliJ telemetry study is presented as measured usage data rather than self-reported preference.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.raw_measurement: Collected (a) vendor-language-neutral survey/telemetry data on Kotlin production usage and (b) named production deployments at large, independently identifiable companies, cross-referenced across multiple independent sources.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.score_rationale: Kotlin has unusually strong, cross-verified production-adoption evidence: (1) it is Google's officially preferred Android language with near-universal presence in top production Android apps, (2) large-scale first-party JetBrains IDE telemetry (not self-report) confirms real-world usage patterns across ~320k developers, (3) named large enterprises (Netflix, Cash App, McDonald's, Forbes, Philips, AWS, Uber, ING, N26, VMware, Duolingo) have publicly documented, multi-year production deployments with quantified scale (millions of transactions/month, 40M+ weekly users, 300+ AWS services), and (4) independent survey channels (Stack Overflow, JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey) corroborate sustained and growing adoption. This is about as strong and well-corroborated as production-adoption evidence gets for a non-C-family/non-Python-tier language. Normalized score: 95/100.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=1-3>The firm is a member of the Kotlin Foundation - the nonprofit that stewards the Kotlin language alongside JetBrains and Google - and its engineers are visible, active contributors to the open-source KMP ecosystem rather than passive adopters of someone else's tooling.</cite>
category_findings.finding: IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio provide first-party Kotlin support; VS Code and other editors have Kotlin plugins. Third-party consultancy Touchlab and others build production Kotlin Multiplatform tooling on top of this stack.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=14-5>Ktlint, developed by Pinterest, is the primary formatting and style linter for Kotlin, known for its zero-configuration approach that enforces the official Kotlin style guide out of the box.</cite> <cite index=15-6>ktlint describes itself as an anti-bikeshedding Kotlin linter with built-in formatter.</cite>
category_findings.finding: ktlint (Pinterest-originated, zero-config) is the dominant Kotlin formatter/style linter; Spotless is a widely used alternative formatter wrapper.

category_findings.category: static analysis / code quality platform integration
category_findings.citation: <cite index=12-1,12-2>Meet detekt, a static code analysis tool for the Kotlin programming language. Visit the project website for installation guides, rule descriptions, configuration options and more.</cite> <cite index=16-3>Third party integrations for Maven, Bazel and Github Actions (Docker based and Javascript based)</cite> <cite index=17-6>Integrations: Codacy, Gradle plugin that configures Error Prone, Checkstyle, PMD, CPD, Lint, Detekt & Ktlint</cite>
category_findings.finding: detekt is a mature, AST-based static analysis tool for Kotlin with a plugin/rule marketplace and integrations into SonarQube, Codacy, GitHub Actions, Bazel, and Maven.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=15-3>The common production setup is ktlint for the formatting gate plus detekt (with a baseline) for the analysis gate, both failing CI.</cite> <cite index=14-12>Most mature Kotlin projects use Ktlint for formatting combined with either Detekt (for non-Android projects) or Android Lint (for Android projects) for deeper analysis.</cite>
category_findings.finding: Industry practice as of 2026 is to combine ktlint (formatting) with detekt (static analysis) or Android Lint, indicating a mature, layered third-party tool stack rather than a single-tool ecosystem.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=29-5>Gradle is the most commonly used build tool in Kotlin, and it provides a Kotlin DSL which is used by default when generating a Kotlin project, so this is the recommended choice.</cite> <cite index=29-6>But you can also use Maven if you are more comfortable with it.</cite>
category_findings.finding: Gradle (with a native Kotlin DSL) is the dominant build tool for Kotlin; Maven and Bazel are also supported, including for Kotlin Multiplatform projects.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=33-2>GitHub now pre-installs Kotlin, if this works for you, there is no need to use this action.</cite> <cite index=35-2>Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Travis CI для автоматизации сборки, тестирования и развертывания.</cite>
category_findings.finding: GitHub Actions has native/pre-installed Kotlin support, and Kotlin projects commonly integrate with GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI, and Travis CI via Gradle/Maven wrapper tasks.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=29-1>the default configuration declares the kotlin-spring plugin which automatically opens classes and methods (unlike in Java, the default qualifier is final in Kotlin) annotated or meta-annotated with Spring annotations</cite> <cite index=32-5,32-6>Ktor is JetBrains' answer to modern, asynchronous backend development. Built from the ground up using Kotlin Coroutines, it is lightweight, flexible</cite> <cite index=21-2,21-3,21-4>JetBrains announces strategic partnership with Spring. The partnership formalizes Kotlin as a first-class citizen. 27% of Spring developers have used Kotlin.</cite>
category_findings.finding: Spring Boot has a formal Kotlin-first-class integration (kotlin-spring plugin, Spring Initializr Kotlin option) and Ktor is JetBrains' own Kotlin-native async web framework, giving Kotlin two mature, widely used server frameworks.

category_findings.citation: <cite index=35-1>Maven Central, JCenter (устаревает), Google Maven Repository, JFrog Artifactory, Nexus Repository Manager.</cite>
category_findings.finding: Kotlin libraries are distributed through Maven Central and the Google Maven Repository, with additional enterprise options (JFrog Artifactory, Nexus, Sonatype).

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Evidence drawn from blog posts, vendor documentation, and GitHub project pages rather than a single authoritative registry; some sources are SEO-style 2026 roundup articles whose company/tool lists could not be independently cross-verified beyond the citations shown.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.raw_measurement: Enumerated the 9 predeclared tool categories for Kotlin and confirmed at least one widely-adopted, actively maintained third-party (non-compiler-team) tool exists and is documented as production-usable in each category.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.score_rationale: Kotlin has a full, mature third-party tool stack spanning every predeclared category (IDE, linter, formatter, static analysis, build systems, CI/CD, frameworks, package repositories, testing), largely because it sits on the JVM/Android tooling ecosystem while also adding Kotlin-native tools (ktlint, detekt, Ktor, KSP). Coverage is broad and depth in each category is strong (multiple competing/complementary tools such as ktlint+detekt+Spotless+Android Lint), though slightly narrower than Java's absolute tool count in some enterprise-legacy niches (e.g. very old APM/profiler integrations built Java-first). Normalized score: 94/100.
